state.request: Enhance Empirical initialization and global agent installation UX. When the empirical-init skill initializes or repairs a repository, present a polished settings wizard before persisting configuration. The wizard must expose evidence policy (required criterion evidence, real-browser checks for UI criteria, UI screenshots, and code review), Git/worktree isolation (mode, base branch, sibling path, and branch pattern), Complex decision records, and any other currently configurable safety settings that belong in setup, while keeping internal Fast/Complex routing hidden. Use safe recommended defaults, explain dependencies between toggles, allow review/edit before confirmation, preserve existing settings during repair, and retain equivalent non-interactive MCP/private-CLI inputs. Replace the current five-row empirical install picker with a searchable, scrollable, polished terminal selector modeled on the current vercel-labs/skills npx CLI experience. Expand global skill-install targets from five agents to the broad audited agent catalog supported by the npx skills ecosystem, including names, ids, native global skill roots, detection hints, and remembered/currently-managed selection. Show detected, installed, and destination-path status; preserve exact --agent, --all, --yes, --json reconciliation and marker/path safety. Keep broad skill-install compatibility separate from executable handoff/MCP capabilities so Empirical never claims it can launch or configure a runtime that only accepts skill files. First produce a reviewable specification and an accurate terminal/conversation mockup; do not implement until the user approves.

evidence.summary: First-run forced-interactive tests prove the full recommended preview precedes persistence, and cancellation leaves configuration and workflow state absent.
Setup, core, and MCP tests cover all four evidence toggles, strict enabled defaults, partial updates, and persistence.

Tests cover every user-facing isolation and decision setting, exclude internal routing/repair limits, and prove required Complex decisions remain enforced independently when code-review evidence is off.
Tests verify criterion-evidence disablement makes UI sub-policies inactive without erasing stored values while code review remains independently enforceable.
Section customization, validation, final review/edit/save, conflicting-mode rejection, and mutation-free cancellation are covered.
Repair tests preserve omitted/current values, preview before mutation, and repair integrations/context only following confirmation.
TypeScript/core, bundled MCP, JSON, and private CLI surfaces accept equivalent partial setup values with correct first-run and repair semantics.
Pure selector and isolated real-TTY checks cover bounded width-safe rendering, scrolling, statuses, path hints, summary, search, required keys, cancellation, and cleanup after render errors.
Catalog tests validate pinned upstream provenance, all 73 global targets, project-only exclusions, safe roots, and offline/no-npx operation.
Tests verify remembered/detected/managed prioritization, label/id/alias/path search, and no implicit select-all.
Integration tests cover five skills per root, 65 deduplicated destinations, reference-safe shared removal, convergence, and unmanaged/symlink/root protections.
CLI/catalog tests cover repeatable --agent/-a, --all, --yes, --json, legacy aliases, remembered selections, manifest migration, and repeated runs.
Tests prove the broad skill registry/type remains separate from the five verified MCP/handoff runtimes and never broadens execution claims.
Human and JSON reports identify agents, unique destinations, filesystem outcomes, skills, verified guidance, and unverified capability boundaries.
Documentation/help/generated skill smoke and npm package dry-run verify the approved wizard and installer contract is shipped without publicizing private workflow commands.
Final source/diff review passes all 15 criteria and all four accepted architectural decisions after the decision-policy independence regression fix.
